problem: Joint world-action navigation models predict action sequences, but the predicted commands can become invalid during execution (dynamic obstacles, occlusion, posture or locomotion-mode changes). Fixed-length or uncertainty-only chunking does not decide how long to follow a prediction.
motivation: Wheel-legged robots have executable motions that depend on both scene geometry and locomotion mode. Long chunks lower planning cost but prolong commitment to stale predictions, while short chunks need frequent costly inference. Prediction uncertainty alone does not capture the consequences of continuing to execute.
key_idea: Separate world-action prediction from execution: choose the longest action prefix (4/8/16) whose calibrated cumulative conditional failure risk stays within a budget, and cancel pending commands whenever new observations invalidate them, treating mode transitions as gated execution boundaries.
insight: Execution length should be a feedback-informed decision combining predictive cues with execution conditions. Full WAVE-Go beats fixed K=4 (74.1 vs 70.1 SR) with 51.2% fewer replans, and beats action-entropy-only and world-uncertainty-only selectors (71.9 SR for the best single-cue one). Removing interruption drops SR by 3.6 points, raises collisions and reaction p95 (0.54 vs 0.21 s), and saves about 18% replans. Fixed K=16 shows that fewer replans and smoother commands do not imply better navigation (66.0 SR, 6.7 collisions).
method: Joint world-action predictor: from the goal image, RGB-D/LiDAR history, motion token, semantic task state and mode, predicts H=16 steps of actions, modes, successor latents and uncertainty/validity cues; trained with future, inverse-dynamics, action, mode and consistency losses
Semantic reasoner: a Qwen-3-VL backbone outputs a fixed-schema task state (progress, evidence, next subgoal, confidence, dependencies), fused with visual features by cross-attention

Conditional-risk prefix selection: a calibrated model estimates per-step failure probability r_t+j (from world-model disagreement, action entropy, obstacle proximity, dynamic-scene evidence, mode status, sensor age); cumulative risk R_t(k)=1-prod(1-r); picks the largest k in {4,8,16} with R<=delta and validity G_t(k)=1, else K=0 (stop and resense)
Interruptible execution: before each dispatch, checks clearance, sensor staleness, task-state change and prediction residual; any violation cancels pending commands and triggers replanning

Evidence-gated hybrid transitions: binary gate over freshness, stability, clearance, goal evidence and controller validity for posture/mode changes; transitions end the prefix and require configuration confirmation and a new prediction

Multi-rate execution: command tracking and checks run at controller rate, world-action inference only when a prefix expires or is cancelled, semantic reasoning when task evidence changes; buffered predictions are revalidated before reuse

setting.backbone: Joint world-action predictor with Qwen-3-VL semantic reasoner (post-trained); Cosmos3-Edge used in the Go2-W real measurement
setting.training_data: Embodiment-specific observation-action transitions for the wheel-legged platform (occlusions, dynamic obstacles, target reacquisition, posture and mode changes), including matched successful and failed transitions; scale not stated
setting.observation: RGB + depth + LiDAR range, proprioception, goal image, optional language
setting.action_space: Hybrid: continuous drive and posture commands plus discrete locomotion-mode events, in prefixes of 4/8/16 commands
setting.simulator: MuJoCo (LUNA); simulator views for Go2-W household and stairs; specific navigation simulator not named
setting.privileged: none stated (SPL uses a shortest feasible reference path for evaluation only)

numbers.eval_set_note: 99 rollouts per method per condition, scene-disjoint splits
numbers.evidence: Table 1: Closed-loop navigation results with 99 rollouts per method per condition

numbers_note: The benchmark is a custom in-house simulation set with no standard benchmark; the simulator and scene names are not given. The 'val' and 'val-unseen' split labels are my mapping of ID and OOD conditions. Collision rate is one number per method, not per condition.
results: WAVE-Go reaches 74.1 ID SR, 68.0 SPL, 64.8 scene-OOD SR and 63.3 dynamic-OOD SR, beating the strongest baseline (NavWAM-style joint W-A: 69.4/63.0/59.7/55.6) by 4.7, 5.0, 5.1 and 7.7 points. Collisions fall from 4.4 to 2.9 per 100 m. Versus fixed K=4 it gains 4.0 SR with 51.2% fewer replans.
limitations: Evaluation is limited to a small custom simulation set (99 rollouts per condition) with baselines re-implemented as '-style' variants; no standard benchmarks or significance tests
The risk budget is an estimated failure budget rather than a certified bound; mode-transition outcomes are not quantified, and the benefit of the predictor adaptation curriculum is not measured
Real-world evidence is only a qualitative station-approach demo and one timing run (0.41 Hz selection rate), so the system runs slowly and interruption adds replanning cost
